questions.question_text: What does the 'final' keyword in Java do?
questions.options_json: {"A": "It prevents a variable from being reassigned.", "B": "It makes a method static.", "C": "It allows a class to be extended.", "D": "It enables autoboxing."}
questions.explanation: The 'final' keyword in Java prevents a variable from being reassigned once it is initialized. This means that the value of a final variable cannot be changed after it is declared.

questions.question_text: What does the 'synchronized' keyword in Java do?
questions.options_json: {"A": "It allows multiple threads to access a shared resource simultaneously.", "B": "It ensures that only one thread can execute a block of code at a time.", "C": "It is used for multithreading and concurrency.", "D": "It is used for garbage collection."}
questions.explanation: The 'synchronized' keyword in Java ensures that only one thread can execute a block of code at a time, preventing data inconsistencies and ensuring thread safety. This is particularly useful when working with shared resources or when multiple threads need to access the same data.
